brief: Gold's multi-year uptrend line is being tested as the metal breaks below its 200-day and 50-day moving averages, with $4,000 the next downside level if the trend line fails. Rising front-end real rates (2-year near a two-year high) raise gold's opportunity cost, and Chinese longs are already liquidating (Shanghai open interest down 11k contracts) ahead of the October 1-7 SHFE holiday, implying more selling into the break. Silver is breaking its 50-day MA too, with $60 the make-or-break level. Separately, the WTI-10-year yield correlation is the tightest in 35 years and the average-stock-to-yield correlation the most negative since 1960, framing oil to yields to equities as the key macro chain; the 10-year is at its most overbought since the 2022 rates panic, while CTAs' asymmetric bond convexity means a yield reversal could spark systematic buying. In equities, institutional and CTA length has been trimmed from record highs, with GS estimating CTAs could buy about $25bn next month, even as traders aggressively chase short-dated upside calls; breadth is at its weakest since the Dot-Com Bubble. France's OAT-Bund spread is widening ahead of any diesel ban, with further gasoil strength a conditional, non-automatic risk to French fiscal spreads.
